questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural banking secure = su ni pa
rural access digital = ze lu su
banking access growth = ze mi ni
secure digital growth = pa mi lu
rural banking growth = ni su mi
What is the code for “rural”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = su, banking = ni, secure = pa, access = ze, digital = lu, growth = mi.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some notes are loans. All loans are deposits. No deposits is a coins.
Conclusions:
I. Some notes are deposits.
II. Some loans are coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few notes are loans. Some loans are deposits. All deposits are coins.
Conclusions:
I. All notes are coins.
II. No loans is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few notes are loans. All loans are deposits. No deposits is a coins.

I. Some notes are not loans.
II. No loans is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All notes are coins.
II. Some coins are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: X = P = R < T = U.
Conclusions: I. U > T   II. U ≥ R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 48 km north, turns left and walks 56 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 70. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 42 km along the initial direction and 56 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(42² + 56²) = 70 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 69 km west, turns right and walks 132 km, then turns right and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 143. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 55 km along the initial direction and 132 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(55² + 132²) = 143 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 163 km east, turns right and walks 270 km, then turns right and walks 19 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 306. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 144 km along the initial direction and 270 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(144² + 270²) = 306 km.

questions.stem: In a queue of 48 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 48 − 22 + 1 = 27.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 44. New front rank = 14+3 = 17. Back rank = 60 − 17 + 1 = 44.

questions.stem: C is the only daughter of D. D is the father of C. H is the son of C. F is the sister of D. How is D related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of C, and C is H’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: G is the brother of H. H is the mother of E. C is the father of G and H. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of E’s mother H. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the mother of G. B is the daughter of G. E is the father of G. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of G, and B is G’s daughter. Hence B is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 54 and 81 hours. An outlet empties it in 135 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 42.63. Net rate = 1/54 + 1/81 − 1/135 = 19/810 tank/hour. Required time = 42.63 hours.

questions.stem: A container holds 170 litres of pure milk. 34 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 108.8. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 170 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 22 people is 39 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 62. New total minus old total = (22+1)×(39+1) − 22×39 = 62.

questions.stem: A boat covers 168 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 68. Still-water speed = 21 km/h. Upstream speed = 21 − 4. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:8. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹52800 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2300 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4472.22. Recover each cost separately: 2300×100/120 + 2300×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

Derived data: A: first category 680, second category 1020; B: first category 1700, second category 1020; C: first category 1020, second category 1360; D: first category 320, second category 480; E: first category 520, second category 780. 480 ÷ 1700 × 100 = 28.24%.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] If the male category at C increases by 20% and the female category there decreases by 10%, what is the new total?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2850. Derived data: A: first category 600, second category 400; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 1520, second category 1140; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 1100, second category 660. 1520 × 1.20 + 1140 × 0.90.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 25.56. Derived data: A: first category 600, second category 400; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 1520, second category 1140; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 1100, second category 660. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?
questions.explanation: Answer: 828. Derived data: A: first category 600, second category 400; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 1520, second category 1140; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 1100, second category 660. Average total = (total A + total E)/2. The second category is 3/5 of that average.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] A fee of ₹20 applies to each in the male category and ₹15 to each in the female category at B. What is the total fee collected (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 43500. Derived data: A: first category 600, second category 400; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 1520, second category 1140; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 1100, second category 660. Fee = 1500×20 + 900×15.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] What is the total number in the male category at A and C together?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2120. Derived data: A: first category 600, second category 400; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 1520, second category 1140; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 1100, second category 660. 600 + 1520 = 2120.

questions.stem: A 220 m train moving at 97.2 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.17. Relative speed = (97.2 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 24 m/s. Time = 220/24.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹23000 earns ₹10350 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 30417.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 23000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 12 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+12)/(x+12) = 3/2 gives x = 12. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3000. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
